# Adapted upstream specification eval contracts

These are offline specification expectations, not executable progress lists or provider transcripts.

## Orchestrator

A new brief creates a TypeScript descriptor, gathers bounded relevant evidence, reviews requirements then solution, surfaces classifier signals, and asks for a tier. Solution-first or requirements-only entry needs explicit omission approval. Resume reads approved content and beads state without rewriting approved sections or creating duplicate task children. Tier overrides retain old artifacts without making them authoritative.

## Requirements

Notification requirements cover distinct personas, MoSCoW scope, journeys, and testable public criteria. Non-UI batch requirements use command output, exit codes, idempotency, and recovery. Sparse briefs trigger user clarification rather than invented scope. Partial documents retain approved sections and resolve only outstanding markers. Requirements contain no implementation architecture.

## Solution

Read public requirements and existing patterns. Compare options and honor a rejected architecture. Confirm choices separately with rationale and trade-offs. Resolve duplicate responsibilities and map every public criterion. No-change refactors do not invent databases or integrations. Resume asks about unresolved decisions without rewriting approved sections. SQL examples verify real schema names and trace conditional behavior.

## Incremental

Define linked static phases, exact file scopes, public references, discovered commands, and test-first acceptance. Validate missing references and orphan phase files without auto-fix. No mutable status fields or task checkboxes are retained.

## Factory

Define self-contained public units, known dependencies, requirement coverage, and separate observable holdout scenarios. At least one P0 scenario covers each unit. User reviews decomposition, holdouts, stubs, and descriptor. Missing solution needs explicit omission approval. Complex dependency chains require valid topological groups. Missing test setup blocks evaluation; it is not skipped success. Public required behavior stays in units; holdout inputs and private outcomes stay separate. Manifest topology is static and task identity belongs to spec.json.
